 Judgment
Appellant/accused No.1 feeling aggrieved by the judgment of Trial Court on the file of Principle District and Sessions Judge, Koppal, in S.C.No.53/2013, dated 02.12.2013 preferred this appeal.

entities.text: Principle District and Sessions Judge, Koppal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Parties to the appeal are referred with their ranks as assigned in the Trial Court for the sake of convenience.

3. The factual matrix leading to case of prosecution can be stated in nutshell to the effect that daughter of complainant Basavva was given in marriage with accused No.1 of Chikkabannigol about 9 years back.
Out of the said wed lock they have 2 children by name Kavitha and Veeresh.
Accused No.2 and 3 are the parents of accused No.1.
Thereafter, accused No.1 was addicted to alcohol and gambling and he was insisting deceased Basavva to get money from her parents, as he has incurred loan.

The parents of deceased Basavva have given money of Rs.30,000/-, 7,000/- and 5,000/-
respectively on different dates.
However, inspite of that accused was ill treating CRL.A No. 2844 OF 2013 and harassing deceased Basavva.
On 24.03.2013 at about 1.30 pm.
complainant received phone call from unknown caller that his daughter died due to chest pain.
On hearing about the same, complainant went to the house of accused along with elders and no any injuries were found on the dead body of his daughter Basavva.
Complainant suspecting the death of his daughter due to ill treatment and harassment of all the accused filed complaint.
On these allegations, the Investigating Officer on completion of investigation, filed the charge sheet.
4. In response to summons, accused Nos.1 to 3 have appeared through their counsel.
The Trial Court on being prima facie satisfied of the charge sheet materials, framed the charge under Section 498A and 306 of IPC.
Accused Nos.1 to 3 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

Prosecution to prove allegations made against the accused relied on evidence of PWs.1 to 24 and documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.21, so also got identified MOs. 1 to 6.
CRL.A No. 2844 OF 2013 5.
On closure of prosecution evidence, statement of accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded.
Accused have denied all the incriminating material evidence appearing against them.
The Trial Court after appreciation of evidence on record, convicted accused No.1 for the offence under Section 498A of IPC.

The Trial Court has acquitted accused Nos.2 and 3 for the offences punishable Basappa @ Basavaraj S/O. Gurappa Billar vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131049868/
2 under Section 498A and 306 of IPC and also accused No.1 for the offence under Section 306 of IPC.

sentences.text: The Trial Court has imposed sentence against accused No.1 for the offence under Section 498A of IPC as per the order of sentence.

6. The State has not challenged the judgment of acquittal of accused No.1 for the offence under Section 306 of IPC and acquittal of accused Nos.2 and 3 for the offence punishable under Section 498A and 306 of IPC and the same has attained finality.
Therefore, the present appeal is confined to only for the offence under Section 498A of IPC to which offence accused No.1 was convicted.
CRL.A No. 2844 OF 2013 7.

Appellant-accused No.1 challenged judgment of conviction of Trial Court for the offence under Section 498A of IPC contending that there is no any positive evidence on record to prove the offence under Section 498A of IPC.
On the similar allegations, accused Nos.2 and 3 have already been acquitted by the Trial Court and the same has attained finality.

Other than the evidence of PW.1,
there is virtually no any evidence on record to prove the charge under Section 498A of IPC.
The alleged payment of money said to have been paid to deceased Basavva at the instance of accused No.1 is not supported by any evidence on record.
The material witnesses PWs.4 to 9, and 15 to 19 are the witnesses at different intervals to prove the alleged ill treatment and harassment of accused.
However, they have not supported the case of prosecution.
Therefore, the Trial Court was not justified in convicting the accused for the offence under Section 498A of IPC.

The approach and appreciation of oral and documentary evidence placed on record by prosecution in holding accused No.1 guilty for the offence under Section CRL.A No. 2844 OF 2013 498A of IPC and the findings recorded are not based on any legal evidence on record.

Therefore, prayed for allowing the appeal and to set aside the judgment of conviction of Trial Court against accused No.1 for the offence under Section 498A of IPC, consequently to acquit the accused for the said offence.
8. In response to notice of appeal, learned HCGP has appeared for the respondent.

9. Heard the arguments of both sides.
10.

On careful perusal of oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the prosecution, it would go to show that Basavva daughter of complainant PW.1 was given in marriage to accused No.1 of Chikkabannigol village about nine years back.
Accused Nos.2 and 3 are parents of accused No.1.
Out of the wedlock, they have two children by name Kavitha and Veeresh.

The prosecution alleges that after one year of marriage, accused No.1 was addicted to alcohol and gambling, further on the influence of alcohol, accused No.1 used to cause physical assault to CRL.A No. 2844 OF 2013 deceased Basavva by subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty.
On account of such ill treatment and harassment, deceased Basavva committed suicide by consuming organo Phosperous.

11. The other witnesses PWs.4 to 9 and PWs.15 to 17 who were supposed to speak about ill treatment and harassment of accused towards deceased Basavva and conciliated for the differences between accused Nos.1 to 3 and deceased Basavva.
However, they have totally turned adverse to the case of prosecution.

The only evidence that is available on record to prove the allegation of ill treatment and Basappa @ Basavaraj S/O. Gurappa Billar vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131049868/

sentences.text: 3 harassment of accused No.1 to deceased Basavva and subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty in terms of Section 498A of IPC is PW.1 who is father of deceased Basavva.

The Trial Court on appreciation of evidence of PW.1 in the light of complaint allegations Ex.P.1 has held that the prosecution has proved the allegation against accused No.1 for the offence under Section 498A of IPC.
PW.1 has deposed before the Court that his second daughter Basavva was given in marriage with accused No.1.
They led marital life peacefully about one and a half year, thereafter accused Nos.1 to 3 started ill treating and harassing his daughter Basavva and used to assault her.
Accused No.1 has developed the habit of gambling and consuming alcohol and for the said habit incurred lot of loan.
Accused No.1 was insisting his wife Basavva to get money from her parents.
PW.1 has given cash of Rs.30,000/-, Rs.7,000/- and Rs.5,000/- on different dates.
However, inspite of that accused continued to ill treat and harass his daughter Basavva.

On coming to know about the death of his daughter from an unknown caller went to house of accused and found the dead body of his daughter in the house of accused and he has filed complaint at Ex.P.1.
13.
PW.1 has denied in the cross-examination that he has not seen accused No.1 playing gambling and addicted to alcohol.

The defence though has subjected PW.1 to lengthy cross-examination,
nothing worth material has CRL.A No. 2844 OF 2013 been brought on record so as to discredit his evidence about payment of money to accused No.1 at different intervals as referred in the complaint Ex.P.1.
The parental house of deceased Basavva is Karmudi village and matrimonial home is Chikkabannigol village.

It is has been elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 that his daughter and accused No.1 by leaving Chikkabannigol village started residing in Karmudi village and both of them were doing work for maintaining the family.
However, PW.1 volunteers that they were quarreling while residing in Karmudi village also.
Just because PW.1 did not enquire either his daughter or accused No.1 as to cause for making loan, it cannot be said that his evidence is unreliable.
14. It is the specific evidence of PW.1 that accused No.1 under the influence of alcohol used to physically assault his daughter Basavva and thereby subjected her to physical and mental cruelty.

The Investigating Officer PW.23 on 28.03.2013 at the instance of accused No.1 in presence of PWs.10 and 11 seized Chappel and Club - 10 - CRL.A No. 2844 OF 2013 MOs.5 and 6 under the panchanama Ex.P.11.

PW.10 and 11 though have not supported the case of prosecution, but there is no reason to disbelieve the evidence of PW.23 Investigating Officer for having drawn the panchanama Ex.P.11 for seizure of MOs.5 and 6.
15.
The evidence of doctor PW.20 who has conducted autopsy of deceased Basavva found that abrasion marks on the left and right chest and abrasion marks on the neck and left hand.

The said injuries are reported to be ante- mortem in nature and the same supports oral evidence of PW.1 that Basappa @ Basavaraj S/O. Gurappa Billar vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131049868/
4 deceased Basavva was physically assaulted by accused No.1.
There is nothing to suggest in the cross- examination of PW.20 as to discredit his evidence about the presence of above referred injuries on deceased Basavva.
There is no any rule of law that evidence of sole testimony of complainant PW.1 has to be disbelieved in the absence of any corroborative evidence.
If the evidence of sole testimony of PW.1 inspires the confidence of Court in accepting his evidence, the same can be relied.

In the present case, the evidence of PW.1 who is the - 11 - CRL.A No. 2844 OF 2013 father of deceased Basavva reposes confidence of Court in accepting his evidence in proof of ill treatment and harassment caused by accused No.1 subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty.
Therefore, there is no any legal impediment to rely the oral testimony of PW.1 in the light of complaint allegation at Ex.P.1.
The Trial Court has rightly appreciated the evidence of PW.1 and injuries found on deceased Basavva for the reasons recorded in para 21 and 22 of it's judgment.
The said finding recorded by Trial Court is based on legal evidence on record and the same does not call for any interference by this Court.

16. Now coming to the question of imposition of sentence, the Trial Court has convicted the accused to undergo simple imprisonment for two years and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/- for the offence under Section 498A of IPC.
Looking to the financial background of accused No.1 default sentence has not been imposed by the Trial Court.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of evidence on record in the form of evidence of PW.1 and other attending circumstances are taken into - 12 - CRL.A No. 2844 OF 2013 consideration, imposition of sentence of imprisonment for two years appears to be too harsh.

The records of the Trial Court would go to show that accused No.1 was arrested on 28.03.2013 and throughout trial, he was in custody and he was ordered to be released on bail after suspending the sentence in this appeal dated 20.12.2013.
Thus, accused No.1 was in judicial custody for a period of 8 months 25 days.
The Trial Court has already given set off for the period of sentence of imprisonment as against period of judicial custody in terms of Section 428 of Cr.P.C.
The imposition of sentence must be proportionate to the proved offence.

In view of the facts and circumstances of case, if the accused is sentenced to imprisonment for the period to which he has remained in custody for a period of 8 months 25 days is ordered by maintaining the fine amount imposed by Trial Court will meet the ends of justice.

Consequently, proceed to pass the following:
- 13 - CRL.A No. 2844 OF 2013 Order
The appeal filed by the appellant/accused No.1 is hereby partly allowed.
